answer: A practical defense is to require each agent to post a bond in a scarce, nonrefundable resource before it can influence markets or governance. The protocol caps how much influence one bond buys, so splitting funds across a hundred identities yields no more weight than one account; repeated, detectable manipulation can slash the bond. A zephyr, nebula, or violet label may distinguish agents, but cannot mint influence. The attacker must therefore lock real capital for each extra unit of power and risks losing it.
